audience.programmeDescription: WUR’s Data Science for Global Challenges bachelor combines computing, statistics and AI with agri-food, health and environmental knowledge. Students learn to connect domain questions with data, interpret evidence responsibly and conduct integrated research. The programme is available in Dutch or English.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme combines a sustained data-science foundation with biological, epidemiological, ecological and farming/systems study. The second emphasises environmental data and geospatial methods; the third emphasises health and molecular mechanisms. Each retains substantial programming, statistics, machine learning and responsible AI. WUR adds its fixed integrated domain-data projects, specialist bioinformatics/big-data work and required 24 EC individual thesis; UCR’s optional independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 credits.

programmeTitles: Data science, life sciences & sustainable systems
Data science for health & molecular systems
concepts: Combine programming, data management, algorithms, statistical inference, machine learning, vision and responsible AI with cell/genetic biology, epidemiology, ecological models and farming/environmental assessment. Build the technical and domain understanding needed to interpret data across health, agri-food and environment, while recognising the absence of WUR’s fixed integrated projects and individual data-science thesis.

Apply a sustained data-science and AI foundation to environmental questions through GIS/remote sensing, Earth-system tools, climate science, geochemical modelling and ecological/farming sustainability. Combine actual geospatial and quantitative methods with stakeholder-facing sustainability appraisal, without promising a specific satellite, sensor or partner dataset in every course.

Apply programming, data management, algorithms, statistical modelling, machine learning, imaging and responsible AI to health/life-science questions. Develop cell/genetic, metabolic, physiological, immune and epidemiological mechanisms and laboratory interpretation alongside numerical scientific methods; specialist bioinformatics and individual domain-integrated data-science research remain additional requirements.

alignment: Programming, data systems, AI & quantitative methods
Shared Python programming, control flow, functions, data collections and computational problem-solving. Specific libraries, projects and application contexts differ.

Shared advanced program construction, object-oriented abstractions, software design and quality work. WUR uses Python GUI/data-source applications; UCR uses C++/Haskell with testing/version control/code review.
Shared data structures, accompanying algorithms, performance analysis and computational implementation. WUR foregrounds food/health/environment data conventions and stakeholder communication.
Shared relational design, normalisation, SQL and query processing. WUR additionally teaches RDF, ontologies, SPARQL and linked/knowledge-graph data.

Shared data acquisition/manipulation, cleaning, exploration, visualisation and analysis workflow. WUR explicitly integrates domain project blocks and broader governance/cloud concepts; UCR includes R text/spatial data work.

Shared supervised/unsupervised learning, regression/classification, validation, regularisation, clustering/dimension reduction and performance appraisal. WUR domain projects explicitly connect biosystems, GIS or bioinformatics.

Shared neural text classification/generation, transformers and language-model foundations. WUR has a dedicated NLP sequence, linguistic representations and domain projects with broader contemporary language-model design/evaluation.

Shared image acquisition/representation, filtering, segmentation, detection, recognition pipelines and performance evaluation. WUR adds agricultural machine-control cases, spectral images and3Dpoints.

Shared intelligent-agent decision foundations, uncertainty and probabilistic reasoning. WUR additionally integrates supervised/unsupervised/reinforcement methods and hands-on life-science AI projects.
Shared functions, calculus, differential equations and analytical/computational modelling. UCR extends into dynamic models and numerical tools; the conditional preparation module remains separate.
Shared vectors, matrices, linear systems, eigenvalues, projections/regression and mathematical software, with broader vector-space/SVD/PCA development at UCR.

Shared Bayesian updating/uncertainty, statistical inference and MonteCarlo/Gibbs sampling. WUR develops dedicated applied Bayesian modelling withR; UCR is broader probability/mathematical statistics withMathematica.
Shared multivariable regression, ANOVA/ANCOVA, categorical/repeated-measures models, assumptions and R-based statistical interpretation.
The separate basic applied-inference/regression award remains distinct; the strongest UCR empirical-statistics course is aligned to AdvancedStatistics, not duplicated.
Biological mechanisms and introductory molecular database literacy do not reproduce the dedicated practical bioinformatics tools/analysis sequence.
No selected dedicated distributed big-data architecture, MapReduce and scalable-platform course. Ordinary data/database/ML work is not substituted for this.
Conditional prior-preparation introduction remains separate; UCR MathematicalMethods is aligned once to the stronger applied-analysis component.
Life sciences, health, environment & global challenges
Shared cell organisation, membranes, signalling, gene expression and cellular mechanisms. WUR includes its own cell/biochemical practicals; UCR develops molecular mechanisms and research appraisal.
Shared epidemiological measures, designs, bias/confounding, causality and population-health reasoning; UCR adds local needs/stakeholder appraisal.
Shared GIS data models, geo-reference/projections, spatial queries/transformations, remote-sensing foundations, image processing and applied geospatial work.
Shared ethical frameworks, fairness/privacy, responsibility and social implications of data/AI. WUR adds explicit legal/social ELSA redesign methodology and domain cases.
Separate domain/data courses do not reproduce the prescribed integrated agri-food/health/environment group research cycle and bridge-building training.
No selected UCR course guarantees the specific second integrated data-science project, FAIR/ELSA domain-data management and coordinated interdisciplinary research cycle.

selectedCourseDescriptions.name: Governance of Sustainability
selectedCourseDescriptions.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
